name: The debt-supply squeeze
thesis: Hypothetical editorial stress case: U.S. federal debt climbs, major foreign Treasury holders do not add to holdings, and inflation and policy rates remain elevated.
fit: A Prism editorial scenario exploring themes in Ray Dalio's public macro work; this is not their forecast.
risk: Debt thresholds and foreign Treasury holdings can diverge; several legs have long settlement horizons.

rows.rationale: Debt reaching $45 trillion anchors the fiscal-supply thesis.
Higher debt threshold adds an intentionally more aggressive tail.
Mainland Chinese Treasury holdings fail to rise, a foreign-demand signal.
Japanese Treasury holdings fail to rise, a second foreign-demand signal.
December 2027 CPI above 3% expresses persistent inflation.
A federal funds upper bound above 4% at 2027 year end expresses rates staying elevated.

name: Stagflationary policy trap
thesis: Hypothetical editorial stress case: inflation remains sticky while jobs and output weaken, with the Fed unable to return to low rates by year end 2027. This is not a claim about Roubini’s actual forecast.
fit: A Prism editorial scenario exploring themes in Nouriel Roubini's public macro work; this is not their forecast.
risk: Stress scenario, not Nouriel Roubini’s stated baseline; inflation and recession legs can diverge.

rows.rationale: An NBER recession in 2027 is the hard-landing anchor.
Real Q1 2027 GDP growth fails to exceed 2%, expressing slower output.
December 2026 unemployment above 4.5% is an early labor warning.
December 2026 headline CPI above 3.5% expresses sticky inflation.
December 2026 core CPI above 3% tests breadth of inflation.
December 2027 CPI above 3% extends inflation persistence.
Federal funds upper bound above 4% at 2027 year end expresses a restrictive policy backdrop.

name: Trade normalization stalls
thesis: Commercial shipping through major Middle East chokepoints remains constrained, energy retains a risk premium, and U.S.–China trade and tariff policy continue to show fragmentation.
fit: A Prism editorial scenario on supply chains and chokepoints, themes in Zeihan’s public work; this is not his forecast.
risk: Several short-dated legs can resolve within days and may move independently; one API expected-expiration field conflicts with the rule cutoff.

rows.rationale: Hormuz 7-day average does not exceed 60 before April 1, 2027; the long-horizon reopening test for the chokepoint thesis.
Weekly Hormuz transit calls stay at 30 or fewer in October 19–25, testing near-term shipping restraint.
No single day in October 19–25 exceeds eight Hormuz transit calls, testing whether a short rebound fails to appear.
Suez Canal transit calls stay at 300 or fewer in the same week, extending the shipping-friction thesis to the Red Sea route.
Brent closes above $108.99 per barrel on October 23, expressing an energy-price premium alongside chokepoint stress.
2026 U.S. goods imports from China finish below $280 billion, a separate annual test of weaker cross-border trade.
A qualifying executive action imposes new or increased tariffs in October, testing continued policy fragmentation.

name: Anthropic’s coding and IPO edge
thesis: Anthropic retains coding leadership and reaches IPO confirmation before OpenAI
fit: A Prism editorial scenario exploring themes in Scott Galloway's public work; this is not their forecast.
risk: Model-ranking and IPO outcomes are correlated; this is not Scott Galloway’s forecast.

rows.rationale: Anthropic finishes the year with the top coding model.
Anthropic confirms an IPO before 2027.
OpenAI does not confirm an IPO in the same window.
Stable Claude pricing reinforces competitive adoption.
OpenAI does not regain a top-ranked model before 2027.

name: Clean power scales across technologies
thesis: Clean electricity scales through nuclear, solar, and storage
fit: A Prism editorial scenario exploring themes in Bill Gates's public work; this is not their forecast.
risk: Horizons range from 2026 to 2030; some energy outcomes may involve companies with which Gates has ties. No trade is proposed on his behalf.

rows.rationale: A new U.S. reactor license is a near-term nuclear milestone.
Illinois nuclear output clears the contract threshold.
U.S. solar deployment reaches at least 45 GWdc.
Tesla energy-product deployments exceed 20 GWh in a quarter before Q1 2027.
A U.S. military-base nuclear-powered data-center project begins construction process by 2030.
Fusion reaches the contract-defined achievement milestone by 2030.

name: Healthcare affordability remains strained
thesis: Healthcare affordability strain persists while federal coverage reforms stall
fit: A Prism editorial scenario exploring themes in Mark Cuban's public work; this is not their forecast.
risk: Insurance and ACA contracts are indirect proxies for healthcare affordability, and policy outcomes may diverge.

rows.rationale: CMS does not add obesity or chronic weight-management GLP-1 coverage to Part D before 2028.
ACA Marketplace effectuated enrollment falls more than 20% year over year.
Enhanced ACA credits are not extended by year-end 2026.
An HSA/FSA-directed subsidy bill does not become law by year-end.
Core ACA provisions avoid repeal through the specified 2029 deadline.

name: Tech platforms face tighter rules
thesis: Governments tighten AI and child-safety rules for technology platforms
fit: A Prism editorial scenario exploring themes in Kara Swisher's public work; this is not their forecast.
risk: Regulatory outcomes differ across jurisdictions and definitions; there is no single common event.

rows.rationale: A U.S. national AI regulator emerges before 2028.
Mandatory independent AI safety audits take effect before 2028.
Federal AI legislation reaches the contract criterion by early 2027.
The U.S. enacts a child social-media ban without a parental-consent bypass before 2027.
A UK under-16 account ban enters into effect before August 2027.
New Zealand makes an under-16 social-media ban law before October 2027.

name: White-collar layoff pressure rises
thesis: White-collar layoff pressure without a national unemployment spike
fit: A Prism editorial scenario exploring themes in Andrew Yang's public work; this is not their forecast.
risk: Layoff announcements and unemployment do not establish AI causation; these are labor-market proxies.

rows.rationale: Alphabet acknowledges a layoff before 2027.
Tesla acknowledges a layoff before 2027.
Nvidia acknowledges a layoff before 2027.
Professional and business services layoffs exceed 5.497 million in 2026.
National U-3 unemployment never exceeds 5.5% for a 2026 month.
